Yesterday someone asked why kvo creates an intermediate class instead of simply overriding the setter to invoke callbacks. method_swizzling is an excellent mechanism and can certainly satisfy observation requirements. But what if the observed object is a tableView? An app normally has more than one list, and method_swizzling would add observation callbacks to every list. Even setting aside the possible crash risk, the setters of all tableView-derived views, including tableView itself, would be affected. An intermediate class avoids this problem.
